title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let \hat\pi_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. It is free on loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1. The symmetry group S_3 acts through two elements:
- ρ, of order 3, permuting l_0 → l_1 → l_∞ (up to conjugation);
- σ_∞ (later written τ_∞), of order 2, fixing ∞ and exchanging l_0 and l_1.
Grothendieck works in the extended group \tilde\Pi = \hat\Pi_{0,3}·{1, τ_∞} and studies "automorphismes à lacets". These are automorphisms u with u(l_0) = int(f^{-1})(l_0^μ), with multiplier μ = 2ν+1 ∈ \hat Z^*.

Previous page. He treated the u commuting with σ_∞. They are parametrized by pairs (ξ, φ) with φσ_∞(φ) = 1, ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 and the compatibility ξ = l_0^ν φ.

This page: the symmetric case, u commuting with ρ (i.e. g = 1). Such u are given by
- (18) u(σ_∞) = hσ_∞ and u(ρ) = ρ;
- (19) u(l_0) = int(f^{-1})(l_0^μ).
The 'formule de Carte' (11) becomes (20) σ_∞(h) = σ_∞(f)^{-1} l_1^ν ρ(f). Applying σ_∞ (which sends l_1 to l_0) gives (21) h = f^{-1} l_0^ν (σ_∞ρ)(f).

The involutivity condition (*) h σ_∞(h) = 1 (from u(σ_∞)² = 1) then becomes an equation in f:
- h σ_∞(h) = f^{-1} l_0^ν [σ_∞ρ(f) σ_∞(f)^{-1}] l_1^ν ρ(f).
- The bracket equals σ_∞(ρ(f) f^{-1}) = σ_∞(ψ^{-1}), with (22) ψ := f ρ(f)^{-1}.
- Conjugating by f, the condition reads l_0^ν σ_∞(ψ^{-1}) l_1^ν ψ^{-1} = 1.
- Inverting: ψ l_1^{-ν} σ_∞(ψ) l_0^{-ν} = 1.
- Conjugating by l_0^{-ν}: (l_0^{-ν}ψ)(l_1^{-ν}σ_∞(ψ)) = 1, i.e. η σ_∞(η) = 1 with (23) η = l_0^{-ν}ψ.

Conclusion (continued on the next page). Loop-automorphisms commuting with ρ correspond to triples (η, ψ, ν) with 2ν+1 invertible. They satisfy the 3-cycle equation ψρ(ψ)ρ²(ψ) = 1 (automatic for ψ = fρ(f)^{-1}, since ρ³ = 1) and the 2-cycle equation ησ_∞(η) = 1, linked by ψ = l_0^ν η. There is one further subtlety: the cocycle ψ must be the coboundary of some f in \hat\Pi_{0,3} itself, not merely in the extended group \tilde\Pi. That is a nonabelian H^1(Z/3, -) issue.

This is exactly the duality between the two Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations. The twist l_0^{ν}, with ν = (λ−1)/2, is the same as the m = (λ−1)/2 exponent in Drinfeld's hexagon relation. The page is the 'dual' half of a symmetric analysis of the centralizers of the two generators of S_3 in the loop-automorphism monoid.
errors: No algebraic errors found. Each step (20)→(21)→(*)→ησ_∞(η)=1 checks, assuming σ_∞(l_1)=l_0 and ρ³=id.

The equation ψρ(ψ)ρ²(ψ)=1 is automatic for ψ=fρ(f)^{-1}. The real content is the converse (every solution is such a coboundary with f in \hat\Pi_{0,3}). This is not addressed on this page; Grothendieck takes it up on the next page.

ideas.what: Parametrizing automorphisms of \hat\pi_{0,3} (with multiplier μ=2ν+1) that commute with the order-3 symmetry ρ by solutions of the 2-cycle equation ησ_∞(η)=1 and the 3-cycle equation ψρψρ²ψ=1, linked by ψ=l_0^νη.
ideas.modern_name: Two-cycle and three-cycle (hexagon) relations of \hat{GT}; the (λ−1)/2 twist
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991); Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984) sketches the program
ideas.where_published: Possibly La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) / Esquisse d'un programme in outline

ideas.what: Writing ψ = fρ(f)^{-1} as a coboundary and asking whether f lies in \hat\Pi_{0,3} or only in \hat\Pi_{0,3}⋊{1,τ_∞}.
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian cohomology H^1(Z/3, \hat F_2) / coboundary parametrization of 3-cycle solutions

ideas.what: Symmetric treatment: centralizer of σ_∞ (previous page) versus centralizer of ρ (this page), each giving the GT-type equations with roles exchanged.
ideas.modern_name: Stabilizers of the S_3-action in the loop-automorphism monoid of \hat F_2

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently derives the GT 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations, with the Drinfeld twist ν=(λ−1)/2 appearing as l_0^ν. He does so by studying automorphisms that commute with only one generator of S_3, in a symmetric 'dual' manner. The separate centralizer problems, together with the coboundary/extended-group obstruction, are a perspective only partially present in the literature.
missed.quote: on trouve que les automorphismes à lacets de \hat\Pi_{0,3} commutant à ρ correspondent aux triples (η,ψ,ν)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents Grothendieck's own route to the GT relations. Mathematically mild: it isolates the half-GT monoids defined by one relation each, and the H^1 obstruction.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct derivation of GT-type relations from the centralizer of ρ, with Drinfeld's (λ−1)/2 twist. It is historically interesting as Grothendieck's independent formulation, but the underlying relations are well known.
transcription_corrections: (18): 'u(φ)=1' should read u(ρ)=ρ (g=1 means u commutes with ρ).
The '∓' after (21) is a stray mark / end-of-formula sign, not a ± symbol.
"L'équation en h" (2): the (*) equation h σ_∞(h)=1 refers to equation (2) of the earlier pages.
